Nikon Preset 0.5.5-beta - Delivery and validation record
Date: 2026-10-17 (Asia/Shanghai)

DELIVERED ARTIFACT

File: dist/nikon-usb-0.5.5-beta-debug.apk
Application ID: com.nikonpreset.usbprobe
Version name: 0.5.5-beta
Version code: 22
APK size: 2736761 bytes
APK SHA-256:
3b2b7235f5e89b9c27f919b6aac39b99d534452bd27a571fae3ca7317a5688a0

The final artifact was installed through ADB with existing application data
preserved on device 286f0dba, model PKG110, Android 16. The installed version
and APK hash matched this artifact. Installation did not change the phone's
permissions or bring the application to the foreground. No real camera was
connected for this delivery validation.

CHANGES IN THIS BUILD

- After an acknowledged, exact-readback-verified wireless preset import, retain
  the owned connection for another explicitly confirmed import.
- An application-owned runtime holds wireless owners, the shared album
  controller, and serial camera work independently of the Activity. Ordinary
  Home navigation, screen off, and Activity recreation do not themselves close
  the connection.
- A connectedDevice foreground service maintains a connection notification and
  a partial CPU wake lock while needed. Read-only heartbeats run approximately
  every 10 seconds: album storage queries on the album worker, Picture Control
  Standard reads on the serial camera worker. File/network-library work uses a
  separate executor so it cannot starve camera heartbeats.
- Explicit disconnect releases the owned connection, stops the service when
  cleanup is complete, and releases its locks. No reconnect or write retry is
  performed automatically.
- Import intent is persisted before calling the registration backend. Unknown
  outcomes remain blocked until the user performs read-only recovery. A later
  connection failure does not turn a previously verified import into a claim
  that it was never written.
- Shared persistence locking protects report and import-journal access across
  the file and camera workers. Old Activity callbacks and invalidated operation
  leases cannot install an obsolete prepared owner.

USER SETUP FOR BACKGROUND / LOCK-SCREEN USE

Open Settings -> Background connection protection -> Allow background running
(Chinese UI: 设置 -> 后台连接保护 -> 允许后台运行), then approve the relevant
system setting. Also allow application notifications so the ongoing connection
notification and its disconnect action are available in the notification drawer.
Some phone vendors additionally require an unrestricted application battery
setting. These phone settings were not changed during APK installation.
Final read-only inspection of the phone found no application entry in the
device-idle whitelist and POST_NOTIFICATIONS granted=false. The manifest's
REQUEST_IGNORE_BATTERY_OPTIMIZATIONS permission being granted only permits the
application to request exemption; it is not proof that exemption was granted.

A foreground service and CPU wake lock improve ordinary background execution;
they do not provide an unconditional exemption from device-wide Doze or vendor
process/network restrictions. A modern Wi-Fi performance lock is not treated as
a guarantee of background or screen-off connectivity.

REGRESSION RESULTS

17832 checks passed in total:
- 9205 core checks.
- 8627 Picture Control probe checks.

These are host/regression checks, not real-camera interoperability results.

INDEPENDENT ANDROID LIFECYCLE / PROTOCOL LOG AUDIT

Artifact tested: exactly the APK hash recorded above.
Environment: Android emulator and a loopback-only synthetic Z6II peer.
The peer stores virtual slots only in memory, exposes zero album photos, and
never accesses camera hardware. It rejects new initialization after CloseSession.
The emulator's battery-optimization exemption was explicitly granted through
the actual Android system Allow UI before the background/Doze checks.

Archived evidence:
- docs/device-review/wireless-0.5.5-background.log
- docs/device-review/wireless-0.5.5-lifecycle.log

Connection and transaction totals, independently recomputed from the log:
- InitCommand: 1; InitEvent: 1; OpenSession: 1.
- Every command used session 1; no second initialization or reconnect occurred.
- 141 commands total, including the initial DeviceInfo and OpenSession at tx 0.
- Positive transaction IDs were exactly 1 through 139, with no gaps or repeats.
- CloseSession: 1, only at the final explicit manual disconnect.
- No reject, socket-error, or server-error entries.
- OpenSession 02:33:53.746Z to CloseSession 02:48:01.782Z: 848.036 seconds.

Read-only heartbeat totals:
- 28 periodic album 0x1004 storage queries, excluding initial enumeration.
- 58 Picture Control Standard reads in all.
- Of those, 2 were initial/refresh reads; 56 were periodic heartbeats:
  20 before the first import, 25 after C1 and before the second refresh,
  2 during the second confirmation, and 9 after C2.
- The synthetic summary's heartbeats=57 includes the second refresh Standard
  read; it must not be reported as 57 periodic Picture Control heartbeats.

Observed lifecycle stages:
1. Album Home interval, 02:35:49.9238916Z to 02:38:01.0372011Z:
   131.113 seconds, with 13 album heartbeats. A clear-task/new-task Activity
   rebuild then restored the connection in the same application process
   (PID 19406), without an additional Init/Open.
2. Album-to-Picture-Control handoff:
   tx31 DeviceInfo, tx32 capabilities, tx33 Standard, tx34-42 all nine slots,
   on the same session. Picture Control heartbeats then continued after Home
   and screen off at 02:38:42.2655712Z.
3. Explicit force-deep-Doze interval with the granted optimization exemption,
   02:39:34.7444713Z to 02:41:34.9750841Z:
   120.231 seconds, with 12 Picture Control heartbeats (tx49-60).
   The system log records forced deep IDLE. A display wakefulness value alone
   was not used as proof of device-wide Doze.
4. First import success page, Home and screen off,
   02:42:08.4156455Z to 02:45:17.1626536Z:
   188.747 seconds, with 19 Picture Control heartbeats (tx78-96).
   Another Activity rebuild restored the verified success and live connection.
5. The user completed the first result, explicitly confirmed C2 using the same
   retained connection, then returned through detail/root to Settings.

Two explicit virtual imports, with no occupied-slot overwrite:

C1 (item 201):
- Fresh DeviceInfo tx63, capabilities tx64, all nine slots tx65-73.
- The target was read again at tx74 before registration.
- One 614-byte registration at tx75; exact target readback at tx76.

C2 (item 202):
- A fresh selection scan at tx102-113 observed C1 occupied.
- Fresh DeviceInfo tx116, capabilities tx117, all nine slots tx118-126.
- The target was read again at tx127 before registration.
- One 614-byte registration at tx128; exact target readback at tx129.
- C1 was read at tx105 and tx118 and still contained its original dataset.

Both writes and their immediate readbacks had this identical SHA-256:
07434caabeee4bc79727b3cbfd105e037659933866e5aada76419db8745bb199

ACK evidence qualification: the synthetic server accepts a write only after the
complete 614-byte dataset and framing have been validated, then sends a same-tx
0x2001 response. The log does not separately dump transmitted ACK frames.
Server source, the following target readbacks, and the application's verified
success UI jointly corroborate acceptance; this is not a packet-capture claim.

Final explicit-disconnect cleanup:
- Settings disconnect was recorded at 02:47:59.4410072Z.
- The sole CloseSession was tx139 at 02:48:01.782Z, after that manual action.
- The synthetic peer reported connections=1, opens=1, closes=1, virtualWrites=2,
  attemptedTargets=[201,202], then closed its transport.
- The system service dump contained no running application service afterward.
- The Nikon partial wake lock had a release record and no active Nikon lock
  remained. The UI showed the camera disconnected.

NOTIFICATION DENIAL AND BACKGROUND TRANSPORT LOSS

A separate read-only loopback peer was started on the same port after the
successful two-import session had been explicitly disconnected. With no live
connection, the emulator notification permission was revoked to reset the test;
this can restart the application and is not counted as a background failure.
The next actual Android notification prompt was explicitly answered Don't allow.
The system package dump records POST_NOTIFICATIONS granted=false, while the
connectedDevice service dump still records isForeground=true and notification 41.
One InitCommand/InitEvent/OpenSession and the complete capability/nine-slot scan
succeeded. Five periodic Standard reads (tx12-16) followed, despite denial.
No registration operation was issued; this peer does not advertise registration.

At 02:50:54.1399578Z the application was sent Home, then the owned loopback server
was stopped to close its transports. The Nikon CPU lock was released at
02:51:02.640Z. Before returning to the foreground, the service dump was empty and
active wake locks were zero. The returned wireless page said the camera was
disconnected, and Settings showed no connection. No automatic reconnect or write
was observed. This tests actual TCP transport loss in the synthetic setup,
not loss of the phone's Wi-Fi radio or a real camera access point.

Evidence: docs/device-review/wireless-0.5.5-loss.log and the lifecycle log.
Screenshots include phone-apple-v055-success-restored.png,
phone-apple-v055-second-success.png, phone-apple-v055-disconnected.png,
phone-apple-v055-notification-denied-connected.png and
phone-apple-v055-transport-lost.png under .impeccable/review/. The root reviewer
inspected the first two captures as actual pixels and checked UI hierarchies for
the remaining states; this is not a full visual/accessibility certification.

TEST RESOURCE CLEANUP

Stopped the two owned synthetic servers. Restored the emulator's original
always_finish_activities and notification grant, unforced device idle and reset
the simulated battery, then shut down the temporary read-only emulator. None of
these test settings were applied to the physical phone.

SCOPE AND LIMITS

This record establishes the tested application's lifecycle and same-session
protocol behavior against a synthetic peer. It is not a new real-phone/camera
import test. In particular, the forced-Doze result applies only to the emulator
with the explicitly granted battery-optimization exemption. It does not prove
unexempt Doze behavior, OEM power management, or a real camera AP's lifetime.

The imports were triggered by explicit foreground confirmations after returning
to the app. Background execution maintained the connection through read-only
heartbeats; it did not initiate automatic registrations.

Force-stop, system process removal, reboot, radio/network loss, or the camera
turning off its AP can terminate the connection. Original TCP sessions cannot
survive process death. A user must reconnect explicitly; unknown import outcomes
must be checked read-only before another write is allowed.

Seamless transfer is supported from an existing album session into Picture
Control. Starting a new album connection after Picture Control still explicitly
releases the previous owner and connects again; reverse seamless handoff is not
part of this build.

This delivery record contains only the completed checks listed above.
